message.content:
In Texas, tenants have a number of statutory rights designed to protect them from unfair treatment and ensure safe, habitable living conditions. Below is an overview of key tenant rights under Texas law (Texas Property Code, Chapter 24) and related statutes: | Category | Key Rights | Practical Implications | |----------|------------|------------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to one month’s rent for a furnished unit, two months for an unfurnished unit.
• Must be returned within 30 days after lease ends, minus deductions for damages beyond normal wear. | Keep records of the deposit amount and any receipts. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must maintain plumbing, heating, electrical, and structural integrity.
• Must keep the premises in a safe condition. | Document any maintenance issues promptly. | | **Repair & Deduct / Rent Withholding** | • If landlord fails to repair major problems, tenant may pay the repair themselves and deduct cost from rent, or withhold rent until repairs are made. | Keep receipts and communicate with landlord in writing. | | **Notice Requirements** | • For non‑payment of rent: 3‑day notice to pay or vacate.
• For lease termination: 30‑day notice for month‑to‑month tenancy.
• For eviction: 3‑day notice for non‑payment, 30‑day notice for lease violation. | Written notices are required; keep copies. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Tenant has the right to live without unreasonable interference from landlord or other tenants. | Report disturbances or harassment. | | **Anti‑Discrimination** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income. | File complaints with the Texas Commission on Human Rights if discrimination occurs. | | **Privacy** | • Landlord must give reasonable notice (usually 24 hours) before entering the unit, except in emergencies. | Keep a log of entries. | | **Lease Terms** | • Lease agreements must be in writing for leases longer than one year.
• Certain terms (e.g., pet policies, subletting) must be clearly stated. | Review lease carefully before signing. | | **Rent Control** | • Texas does not have statewide rent control; however, local ordinances may apply. | Check city ordinances for any local rules. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must follow the proper legal process: serve notice, file an unlawful detainer action, obtain a court judgment. | Tenants can contest eviction in court. | | **Security Deposit Deductions** | • Landlord may only deduct for unpaid rent, damage beyond normal wear, or cleaning costs if specified in lease. | Dispute unjustified deductions. | | **Subletting** | • Tenants may sublet with landlord’s written consent; landlords cannot unreasonably deny. | Obtain written permission. | | **Pet Policies** | • Landlords may require a pet deposit or fee; cannot refuse pets unless they are service animals. | Provide documentation for service animals. | | **Maintenance of Common Areas** | • Landlord responsible for common areas (hallways, elevators, etc.) to be safe and clean. | Report hazards. | ### How to Protect Your Rights 1. **Document Everything** – Keep copies of all communications, receipts, photos of damage, and a written record of any verbal agreements. 2. **Know the Law** – Familiarize yourself with the Texas Property Code, especially Sections 24.001–24.999. 3. **Use Written Notices** – When giving notice to the landlord or responding to a notice, use certified mail or another method that provides proof of delivery. 4. **Seek Legal Assistance** – If you face eviction or disputes over deposits, consider contacting a local tenant advocacy group or a lawyer who specializes in landlord‑tenant law. 5. **File Complaints** – If you suspect discrimination or illegal eviction, file a complaint with the Texas Commission on Human Rights or the Texas Attorney General’s Office. ### Resources - **Texas Property Code** – Chapter 24 (https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/Docs/PR/htm/PR.24.htm) - **Texas Commission on Human Rights** – https://www.tchra.org/ - **Texas Attorney General – Housing** – https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov/ - **Local Tenant Advocacy Groups** – Search for “tenant rights Texas” for city‑specific resources. --- **Disclaimer:** This information is for general informational purposes only and does not constitute legal advice. For specific legal questions, consult a licensed attorney in Texas.
